column3: The Hebrew calls the stones “whole” and says no one waved iron over them; BSB has “uncut” and the passive “no iron tool has been used.”
The Hebrew uses an unnamed subject and repeats the writing verb; BSB explicitly names Joshua and varies “inscribed” and “written.”

The Hebrew names “the ark” first and later “the ark of the covenant of the LORD”; BSB gives the full designation first and then uses “it.” The Hebrew uses singular collective “foreigner” and “native”; BSB has plural “foreigners and citizens.”
The Hebrew uses an unnamed subject and singular “the blessing” and “the curse”; BSB names Joshua and has plural “blessings” and “curses.”
The Hebrew describes the foreigner as singular and walking among them; BSB uses plural “the foreigners” and says they “lived” among them.
